x.around: Generally, Bratislava is a walking city, though as of the early 2020s with increasing number of cycling lines. The centre is very small and cosy and you can easily walk from one side to another in a few minutes. The city centre is a pedestrian zone, but be aware of cyclists and occasional cars that can sometimes drive rather quickly in between the pedestrian area and outdoor cafes.

hidden.d: The Old Town Hall and Apponyi Palace is open to the public as a museum, with an exhibition of city history.
Gallery of modern Slovak art from the late 19th century, in a building reminiscent of the New York Guggenheim.
Permanent archaelogical collections.
Including the museums of history and music as well as the city dungeon and the exhibition on medieval justice.
Echoing the communist era, the natural science exhibitions have an interesting collection of artifacts and is slowly being transformed into a modern era exhibition.
Rebuilt in the classical style in the 19th century by Count John Pálffy. Part of the Bratislava City Gallery.

x.intro: Bratislava (Hungarian: Pozsony, German: Pressburg, known as Prešporok before 1919), is the capital and largest city of Slovakia. It has a population of more than 475,000 (2021), and is the administrative, cultural and economic centre of the country. For most visitors, it is the entry point into the rest of the country.

must.d: The castle contains a Museum of Bratislava History, and a baroque garden. There is also a restaurant open till after the actual castle tours into the night.

A bridge over the Danube river, with its flying saucer-shaped structure housing a restaurant called "UFO". There is an observation deck on its roof, open from 10:00-23:00 daily, offering great views of the old town, as well as…
There has been a fortress on this site since Roman times. In the 19th and early 20th century it became a Slovak national symbol.

The largest and one of the oldest churches in Bratislava, situated below Bratislava Castle. The Gothic cathedral, formerly the coronation-church of several Hungarian kings, begun in 1204, and reconsecrated in 1445, was restored…
Nicknamed the Blue Church (Modrý kostolík), this is a beautiful Jugendstil church finished in 1913.

On the top of the hill behind the castle, overlooking the entire city. This is a monument in memory of Soviet casualties in the liberation battle of Bratislava in World War II.
This 51-m-high tower above the gate with its green copper roof is one of the best known and the oldest buildings in Bratislava. It was built in the 14th century as one of the four gates to the city.

next.d: on the southern slopes of the Small Carpathians there are extensive vineyards and typical wine villages and towns like Rača, Pezinok or Modra.

x.safe: Bratislava is generally very safe by Western standards. It is quite small and the crime rate is low. There is a significant police presence in the city, especially the historical parts, and it is generally not a problem to walk around the city at night. The centre especially is under camera surveillance.

cities.d: was one of the most important mining towns of Hungarian part of Austro-Hungarian Empire; beautiful restored square, many churches, castles and museums and memorial of the Slovak National Uprising

x.around: Banská Bystrica is a walkable city and all the main sights can be reached by foot in 15 minutes.

The baroque pillar was built in 1719 as a sign of gratitude to the Virgin Mary after the end of the plague.

This house belonged to a medieval miner who built this enormous house beside the town square. Now it hosts information centre of the city and it is also used for the representative purposes of the mayor.
Built around 1552 as a part of the Town market. Entrance fee to the top is €2 (children go for free).
This park at a "center of independent culture" may be closed or used for different happenings.

x.intro: Banská Bystrica is a city in Central Slovakia between the national parks Great Fatra and Low Tatras (north of the city), the national park Poľana (east of the city), and the Štiavnické Vrchy (southwest of the city).

must.d: Baroque style Roman Catholic church, built in the early 18th century.

x.around: Košice has a small and compact city centre, and is mostly navigable by foot. If you are staying in the suburbs, the tram system is cheap and efficient. With good bus and tram connections around the whole city, transport is very easy to handle. You can get practically anywhere by public transport and all the main sights of the city are within walking distance.

hidden.d: A pool 50 m in length with eight lanes and another 25 m in length with four lanes. Sometimes they're reserved for swimming clubs, in that case you can ask if there's a free lane.
A popular park area and easily approachable weekend hangout for many locals. Tennis, playgrounds for children, summer swimming pool, pubs and lovely evening walks by the river.
The final resting place for many important and wealthy personalities in the city, and many tombstones are quite impressive.
A museum presenting the different crafts that were practiced in the region in the Middle Ages, that also contributed to theur development.

The archbishop of Eger was exiled in Košice for a long time in the 17th century, but in 1804 the city got its own bishop and four houses next to the cathedral was transformed into a bishop's residence.
Constructed in 1776, renovated in the 1970s after degradation, nowadays a venue for private parties but you can look at it from the outside.
Cultural Center in old barracks completely renovated in 2013 including the park that surrounds it. Offers concerts, exhibitions and conferences.

x.intro: Košice (pronounced Ko-shi-tse) is the second largest city in Slovakia, with a population of almost 240,000 (in 2021). It was the European Capital of Culture in 2013. Despite its relative remoteness, you may likely find Košice a hidden, unknown and approachable gem when seeking for a lesson in less known European history, lively arts scene or for a less spiritual entertainment thanks to its vibrant party scene.

must.d: A statue of the Hungarian writer born in 1900 in Košice, sitting on a chair facing an empty chair and a pedestal behind him.
This remarkable medieval monument was built in the High Gothic style. The present cathedral stands on a site formerly occupied by a parish church, which was destroyed by fire around year 1370.
The theatre was built in a new-baroque style during the years 1879-1899, according to the projects of A. Lang and A. Steinhardt, where a former theatre building, built in 1788 - 1790, was situated.
Greek-Catholic church in Neo-Romanesque style built between 1882 and 1898. The iconostasis and chair were installed in 1901, and the church was elevated to cathedral status in 2008.

x.safe: While Košice is a generally safe city, it’s advisable to avoid certain areas late at night, such as parks and the vicinity of the train station. As with any urban area, exercise caution in places where there might be a concentration of homeless individuals. If you need assistance, you can always call 112 for emergency medical, police, or fire department services.

x.intro: Poprad is a major tourist and economic centre in the Prešov region of Eastern Slovakia.

x.intro: Žilina is a town in Central Slovakia with a population of 80,000 (2024) and the capital city of the Žilina self-administrative region. The city itself offers a nice historic centre, which is unique in Slovakia thanks to the arcades on the main square, and a vibrant cultural scene. The surrounding region is a paradise for hiking and skiing, with the Little Fatra mountain range being one of the nature hotspots of the country.

must.d: The ruins of the 3rd largest castle of Slovakia.
Beautiful 13th-century castle with a nice park on the confluence of two rivers. It is the seat of Považské Museum, which covers the history of Slovak tinkers and their crafts.
Roman Catholic church from the 15th century, one of the town's most significant monuments and seat of the bishop of the Diocese of Žilina. Locals call it simply the "Parish Church" (Farský kostol).

must.d: It is a symbol of Slovak feudalism, built in the 14th century. It is part of Slovak national heritage.
The oldest architectural monument in Žilina, it dates back to the 13th century. Today, it is located in an industrial area. Take trolleybuses no. 1, 6, 7 or 16 to "Závodská" stop.

intro: "SK" redirects here. For the Canadian province, see Saskatchewan; for the Republic of Korea, see South Korea. Slovakia (Slovak: Slovensko) or the Slovak Republic (Slovenská republika) is a country in Central Europe. The main reasons to visit Slovakia are its natural beauty, vivid history and great opportunities for relaxation (and due to the small size of the country, it is quite easy to combine all three).

x.intro: Levoča is a town in the Prešov Region of eastern Slovakia with a population of 14,700 (2016). The town has a historic centre with a well preserved town wall, a Renaissance church with the tallest wooden altar in the world, carved by Master Paul of Levoča, and many other Renaissance buildings. The town is known in German as Leutschau and in Hungarian as Löcse.

other.d: the most visited castle in Slovakia, almost intact with beautifully preserved interiors.

hidden.d: A mineral water spa with temperatures from 28 to 52 ºC . It springs from 9 wells with a discharge of 40 litres per second from the depth of 1200-1500 metres.
It is one of the oldest monuments in Slovakia; it has become the national museum. The last owner of the castle was the earl Jan Frantisek Palffy.

This is the oldest, but also one of the most modernised zoos, not only in Slovakia but also in central Europe. It offers a lot of fun for children and adults, with beautiful parks, with many species of trees from every corner of…

x.intro: Bojnice is a small town (of population about 5000) in central Slovakia, adjacent to the city of Prievidza.

must.d: 11-m-long cave almost in the city centre, with rich history - people have lived here approx. 40000-70000 years ago. The nearby museum displays the artifacts found here.

x.around: Piešťany is known as a town of cyclists. The town is not very big and to get from one place to another does not take a lot of time. That is why the inhabitants prefer to use bicycle rather than car and traffic jams are rare in Piešťany.
x.intro: Piešťany is a city in the Trnava region of Western Slovakia, on the river Váh, approximately 80 km from Bratislava, the Slovak capital, and 150 km from Vienna.

must.d: First settlements of this area are 24000 year old, but the most important role of the place was during Grand Moravia.

other.d: is a spa town in North-Eastern Slovakia that exhibits numerous cultural monuments in its completely intact medieval town center and is one of UNESCO's World Heritage Sites.

hidden.d: Built in 1505. The lower part was built in the Gothic style, while the upper part was finished in the Renaissance style.

x.intro: Bardejov is a town in North-Eastern Slovakia. It is situated in the Šariš region and has about 33,000 inhabitants. The spa town, mentioned for the first time in 1241, exhibits numerous cultural monuments in its completely intact medieval town centre. The town is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

must.d: Used to be the town’s medieval marketplace, now surrounded by well-preserved Gothic and Renaissance burghers’ houses.
A monumental church, mentioned for the first time in 1247. A three nave basilica with multiple chapels was completed in 1464. It hosts eleven precious Gothic winged altars with panel paintings.
These date from the 14th and 15th centuries and are listed by the European Fund of Cultural Heritage as one of the most elaborate and best preserved medieval fortifications in Slovakia.

n.en: The fortification system and town walls

must.d: This UNESCO World Heritage Site is a Roman Catholic wooden church with a Lutheran past from 15th century. This is the oldest wooden church and the best preserved in Slovakia. The building was built in a Gothic style.
